proposed_from.topic: Simultaneous selected-training TWSF conditional-mean bands with a variance-share Gaussian-complexity frontier. Condition on latent factors and assignments in balanced, strongly identified fixed-rank panels with independent homoskedastic Gaussian cell errors, deterministic direct and recursive training cells, one common terminal W block and forecast origin, and selected-design recovery through H. Derive stacked orthogonal scores and observable positive-semidefinite Gram covariance estimates; prove uniform feasible multiplier-band coverage when (kappa+1)epsilon+(kappa+1)^2t+d tends to zero, with explicit PCR/Riesz/Jacobian rates admitting H=floor(n^(1/8)). Let nu_min be the minimum standardized variance share of independent direct lead responses. Prove bounded recursive complexity and direct complexity comparable to 1+sqrt(nu_min log(2H)) on the declared fixed-rank class. On the persistent all-ones subclass, prove kappa_rec tends to sqrt(2/pi), kappa_dir/sqrt(log H) tends to one, and probability and expected maximum-width lower bounds for uniformly honest rectangles centered at the direct leading Gaussian estimator. Consumer: mlsynth TWSF path ribbons and Shen's NFL-stadium conditional-mean paths; exclude prediction bands and unrestricted-estimator minimax claims. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The stacked S12/S13 score and Gram-covariance formulas were derived. On the legal common-origin all-ones sequence, alpha*=1_L/L, J_ell'1=c_ell1, ||g_ell||^2=1/L+O(H/L^2), direct independent variance share is 1/(2+3/n), kappa_rec approaches sqrt(2/pi), and kappa_dir/sqrt(log H) approaches one. A conditional Gaussian event and sixteen-term remainder ledger yield epsilon_rec=O(H log(nH)/sqrt(n)+H^2 log(nH)/n) and normalized correlation error O_p(H^2 sqrt(log(nH)/n)), so H=n^(1/8) is nonempty. Checks covered selected-training failure, vanishing shares, singular correlations, studentization, long horizons, prediction shocks, randomized widths, and prior-art collapse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Package the displayed events into one class-uniform conditional probability bound with constants depending only on declared class radii, independently auditing spectral perturbation and exceptional-event conventions. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the three-piece perturbation bound for qhat_ell=Zhat_dagger Jhat_ell' W' betahat and the actual-PCR relative covariance rate on the all-ones sequence; pivot if an order-one normalized term or oracle W/Jacobian is required. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The exact causal comparator is Shen (2026), whose Corollary 2 is pointwise and whose Section 6 deliberately reduces each prespecified fixed-horizon summary to a scalar before inference. The explicit \(H_n=1\) singleton-menu inclusion recovers that published result only as validation. The proposed theorem instead retains an \(H_n\)-vector, handles independently selected training from a fixed deterministic menu, and proves a feasible relative Gram rate for the actual fitted PCR, Riesz, terminal-block, and companion-Jacobian objects. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest architecture comparator: it derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts and shows that their ranking depends on lag-order specification. Bhansali (1997) and Ing (2003) establish the broader direct-versus-plug-in MSPE comparison in autoregressive time series. Those predictive results motivate, but neither imply nor are sharpened by, the proposed causal selected-training score, Gaussian maximum and variance-share frontier, feasible Gram covariance, and simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon. Belloni et al. (2018) and Chernozhukov et al. (2015, 2017) provide the final orthogonal-score and Gaussian-comparison tools but do not supply this panel-specific linearization. The second theorem-level object, \(\rho_n\), aggregates heterogeneous lead-specific independent variance shares and gives the correct two-sided direct-complexity law alongside uniform bounded recursion; \(\nu_{\min,n}\) alone yields the simpler law only when the shares are uniformly comparable. No result in the verified TWSF, panel-VAR forecasting, autoregressive multistep forecasting, low-rank panel-inference, PCR, or simultaneous-band threads subsumes either the feasible growing-path theorem or this heterogeneous variance-share frontier.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Section 6, Appendices S12--S13, and the Conclusion were read in arXiv version 3.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Appendix S12 collapses a fixed direct summary to one regression and Appendix S13 propagates one fixed recursive summary; the first changed step is to retain every lead before aggregation and control the selected \(H_n\)-vector and its fitted covariance jointly.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{selected TWSF path},\text{multiplier hyperrectangle}\}\) was searched against Belloni et al. (2018), Chernozhukov et al. (2017), Li et al. (2024), and Choi et al. (2024); none contains the TWSF-specific growing-path construction.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Belloni et al. (2018) after calling each lead an orthogonal target.
seed_details.rebuttal: That theorem assumes a controlled score family; here the leading score, observable covariance, selection map, and uniform PCR/Jacobian remainders must first be derived from one reused noisy panel, including singular correlation.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Adapt the uniform Bahadur-to-multiplier arc of Belloni et al. (2018), but replace empirical score covariance by a coefficient-based positive-semidefinite Gram map whose perturbation is proved for the actual fitted TWSF objects.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 6.3 and Appendices S12--S13 were read; they compare direct and recursive pointwise constructions without analyzing their joint Gaussian maxima.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed proof step is to keep the common-score subspace and the independent direct response contribution separate after standardization, rather than reducing the horizon to a fixed scalar summary.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{TWSF covariance geometry},\text{Gaussian maximum complexity}\}\) was searched against Chernozhukov et al. (2013, 2015, 2017) and no panel-structural scalar frontier was found.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the standard bound \(\mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H}|Z_\ell|\asymp\sqrt{\log H}\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The work is to derive the decomposition with a fixed-dimensional common component and independent share \(\nu_{\min,n}\) from TWSF scores and to prove bounded recursion on the full declared class; generic maximum bounds do not supply either structural fact.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Use arbitrary-covariance comparison only after an exact TWSF score decomposition isolates lead-specific direct innovations from a common fixed-rank Gaussian subspace.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The pointwise interval in Corollary 2 and the conditional-mean NFL path in Section 8.2.2 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to retain the direct leading Gaussian location experiment and turn simultaneous honesty into a maximum event before allowing data-dependent, asymmetric, or randomized coordinate widths.
seed_details.destination_search: The pair \(\{\text{TWSF-centered rectangles},\text{random maximum-width lower bound}\}\) was checked against Cai et al. (2014), Chernozhukov et al. (2014), and Armstrong and Koles\'{a}r (2018); those results concern different function classes or decision geometries.
seed_details.red_team: A trivial consequence of Gaussian quantiles and therefore not a research result.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial content is the legal TWSF embedding with exact independent variance share and the uniform quantifiers over data-dependent and randomized widths; the claim is deliberately restricted to the direct leading-Gaussian center.
seed_details.key_inspiration: Borrow honesty-to-testing logic from Cai et al. (2014), but exploit the simpler exact Gaussian location reduction available on the TWSF persistent subclass.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorems 4.1--4.2, Section 4.3, and the Conclusion were read in the JMLR paper.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to perturb an entire cross-lead Gram matrix after multiplying PCR directions by fitted Riesz maps, noisy terminal histories, and companion Jacobians.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located for \(\{\text{actual TWSF PCR},\text{relative max-norm covariance}\}\).
seed_details.red_team: A routine polarization of existing PCR prediction bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: Prediction error does not control studentized pairwise Gram entries when the marginal variances are of order \(n^{-1}\) and the recursive direction contains an estimated Jacobian and noisy terminal block.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 8.2.2 and Figure 4 were read; the application displays cumulative conditional-mean paths with pointwise intervals.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to left-multiply the daily score and Gram map by the cumulative-sum operator and re-audit variance floors and remainders.
seed_details.destination_search: No cumulative TWSF simultaneous-band theorem was located.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate linear transformation of the daily path theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection largely holds once the daily covariance theorem exists, so this is retained only as a consumer corollary and not selected as a kernel.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, orthogonality construction, Theorem 2.1, multiplier corollary, and proofs of the Gaussian coupling steps were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to form one score stack over both TWSF architectures and every risk-tied training candidate before projecting to the selected path.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper located for \(\{\text{direct-recursive TWSF mode selection},\text{joint multiplier envelope}\}\).
seed_details.red_team: Generic post-selection simultaneous inference already covers the selected coordinate.
seed_details.rebuttal: The score family is not i.i.d. and its members share estimated spectral objects, but the required joint cross-mode covariance is not yet derived; feasibility is therefore lower than for independently selected training within a prespecified mode.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Sections 2--4, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1, their bootstrap proofs, and the Conclusion were read from arXiv version 2202.12078 and the Journal of Econometrics article record.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace the homoskedastic coefficient Gram by a residual-weighted cross-lead covariance while controlling reuse of cells in fitted factors.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair \(\{\text{heteroskedastic growing TWSF path},\text{residual-weighted multiplier}\}\) was not occupied by the panel-bootstrap papers checked.
seed_details.rebuttal: A single panel does not provide repeated score vectors and fitted factor dependence invalidates a naive sandwich; nevertheless this angle is excluded from the present homoskedastic topic.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The fixed-horizon statements and companion-matrix derivative argument in Appendix S13 were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace fixed-horizon derivative constants by sharp powers of \(H_n\) and construct a matching failure sequence at the first nonvanishing normalized covariance term.
seed_details.destination_search: No sharp maximal-horizon theorem for causal TWSF was found; time-series direct-recursive comparisons do not use the same panel score experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The exponent is an artifact of loose Taylor bounds and thus not a structural frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection is unresolved; this seed becomes the paper's open-ended question rather than a promised theorem.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Sections 2.2--2.3, Theorem 3.1, Appendix D, and the Conclusion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to make the TWSF score and Gram map stable to deliberate rank overestimation at every lead.
seed_details.destination_search: Rank-robust low-rank inference exists, but no selected growing TWSF path result was located.
seed_details.red_team: Subsumed by Choi et al.'s later diversified-projection rank-robust inference.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their target is a low-rank linear functional, not a recursive prospective path, but this angle changes the fixed-rank brief and is not selected.
